pattern.crimePattern: indebted camp owner kills the neighbour who bought her mortgage and came to take her camp, and lets the river carry him to the crocodiles
pattern.notes: Fictional camps and owners. Crocodile and hippo behaviour is described only as the pathologist's findings; no image of the body. Camp mortgages and debt purchase are given in outline.

ob.text: Guides report a man's body in the Mara River at crossing point 2 at 08:40, with crocodiles feeding. He is identified as Richard Ainsworth (55), owner of Ainsworth River Camp. Recorded as drowning; crocodile attack suspected.

people.name: Richard Ainsworth
people.bio: Born in Narok to a family three generations in Kenya. Walks everywhere on the bank track, torch in hand.

locations.name: Crossing point 2, Mara River
locations.description: A wide brown crossing where the wildebeest come down in July. In February the water is slow and shallow over coarse yellow sand and gravel; crocodiles bask on the sandbanks. Guides' vehicles stand on the high bank.

hotspots.label: The water's edge
hotspots.text: Rangers have brought the body to the bank under a tarpaulin.

hotspots.label: The crossing bed
hotspots.text: Coarse yellow sand and gravel. Amani bags some.

image.brief: a wide brown crossing on the Mara River in the dry season, coarse yellow sand and gravel banks, crocodiles basking on a sandbank, safari vehicles on the high bank above, no people in focus

locations.description: Tents on the high bank under fig trees, a dining tent, Richard's office with a filing cabinet and a radio.

locations.name: Mara Bend Camp
locations.description: An older camp on a bend upstream, its wooden viewing deck built out over a hippo pool. Below the deck the water barely moves; fine grey silt settles on the bottom. A guest gate with a book on the road side.

hotspots.label: The hippo deck
hotspots.text: The mvule railing along the deck. One post is pale raw timber; the boards are freshly swept.

hotspots.label: Under the deck
hotspots.text: Fine grey silt from the slow pool under the deck. Amani bags some.

facts.text: Richard Ainsworth's body was found in the Mara River at crossing point 2 at 08:40, with crocodiles feeding. Recorded as drowning; crocodile attack suspected.
Recovered from the water at crossing point 2 at 08:40.
Inside his shoes and trouser turn-ups: fine grey silt.
Olekina: he found the body at 08:40 among crocodiles at crossing point 2 and radioed it on the sightings channel.
Olekina was with his clients at their lodge until the 06:00 gate opening; the gate log has his vehicle out at 06:05.
The bed at crossing point 2 is coarse yellow sand and gravel.
Mumbi: at 21:00 Richard left on foot along the bank track. "I'm going to see Mama Lucia about the letter. Back in an hour." He never came back.
Mumbi hosted the guests at dinner in the dining tent until 23:00.
Mumbi: the two camps sent each other guests for years and had Christmas dinner together. "Until the letter."
Richard's letter to Lucia, Thursday: he has bought her camp's debt from the bank. "Pay the full balance by Friday or I take possession of Mara Bend Camp."
Conservancy lease maps in Richard's file: the two camps share no boundary in dispute.
Ainsworth booking records: no booking dispute with Mara Bend Camp, ever.
Staff file: Kipchumba Kemei, bar manager, dismissed on Monday 2 February for theft from the bar.
Mara Bend's hippo deck: one mvule railing post freshly replaced with raw new timber; the old post is missing. The boards have fresh sweeping marks.
The still hippo pool under Mara Bend's deck settles fine grey silt.
Mara Bend's guest gate book: no entry after 18:00. The bank-track path reaches the deck without passing the gate.
Records, Richard's line: Mara Bend mast zone 21:12–21:50, then nothing. The phone was later found in the river.
Josephine: Lekishon sat at the gate fire by her kitchen all night, 100 m from the deck. She brought him tea at ten and at midnight.
Narok hotel bill: Kipchumba checked in at 19:30 on Sunday; his bar tab runs until 01:10.
Airstrip log: last landing 17:40 on Sunday; no movement until 10:00 Monday.
In Mara Bend's workshop, under a tarpaulin: the old mvule railing post, wet and scrubbed, with a crack at one end.
Autopsy: a heavy blow to the head with a wooden object, before death. Splinters of mvule hardwood in the wound.
Autopsy: no water in the airways. He didn't drown.
Autopsy: the crocodile injuries were made after death. No hippo bite or crush injuries.
Autopsy: death between 21:15 and 22:30.
Lab: the splinters are mvule and match the cracked end of the old post. His blood is in the crack.
Lab: the silt in his shoes is from the hippo pool under Mara Bend's deck, not the coarse sand of crossing point 2.

Lucia admits Richard came and they talked on the hippo deck. "He told me my camp was his now. I told him to leave."
Lucia: "He was standing on the deck when I went in."

Lekishon: Mr Richard came along the river path at quarter past nine. In the morning Mama told him to say no one came.

topics.reply: Crocodiles take what the river brings. This one came from upstream. The water is slow; he floated.

timeOfDeath.note: On the deck from 21:15; his phone went into the river at 21:50. The autopsy allows 21:15–22:30.

proof.concludes: Richard didn't drown, and the crocodiles came after death. He was struck with mvule hardwood and went into still water that leaves fine grey silt, not the coarse sand of the crossing.
He walked to Lucia's camp and was there from 21:12; Lucia told her askari to deny it and admits they talked on the deck. His phone went silent at 21:50.
The deck's mvule post was replaced overnight; the old one, cracked and scrubbed, carries his blood and matches the splinters. He died on the hippo deck and the river carried him 2 km to the crossing.
He had bought her debt and come to take her camp. At the hippo deck, Lucia Wanjiru struck Richard with a railing post and left him in the river.

He left his own camp alive at 21:00.
His phone was at Mara Bend from 21:12 to 21:50, and the silt is from the pool under the deck.
Nothing moved at the airstrip; his phone never left Mara Bend.
Kipchumba was in a Narok hotel bar from 19:30 to 01:10.
Lekishon sat at the gate fire by the kitchen all night, 100 m from the deck.
Mumbi hosted dinner at Ainsworth Camp until 23:00.
Olekina was at his clients' lodge until the 06:00 gate opening.
The crocodile injuries came after death.
No hippo bite or crush injuries.
Splinters from a worked railing post, not a branch.
That's Kipchumba's grievance, and he was in Narok.
The lease maps show no boundary in dispute.
No booking dispute was ever recorded.
The camps were friends for years; the letter gives the real reason.

reconstruction.text: Mara Bend Camp is mortgaged. In January Richard quietly buys Lucia's debt from the bank. On Thursday he writes: pay in full by Friday, or he takes possession.
Friday passes. On Sunday at 21:00 he walks along the bank track "to see Mama Lucia about the letter". At 21:15 the askari sees him come along the river path.
On the hippo deck he tells her the camp is his. She picks up a loose railing post, waiting for repair, and strikes him. He falls into the still pool below.
She sweeps the boards, has the post replaced at first light, and hides the old one under a tarpaulin. In the morning she tells Lekishon that no one came.
The slow river carries Richard 2 km downstream. At crossing point 2 the crocodiles find him at dawn. Dr. Chebii: "Your crocodile arrived for breakfast, Detective, not dinner."

clockPlan.note: Records on Richard's phone, then a warrant on the workshop. Wood and silt both take 8 h. No detention needed.
